A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Kaleido research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original architecture ablations, novel-view synthesis experiments, and GSO-30 reconstruction results, with additional quantitative results in Appendices A and C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds camera-conditioned video comparisons in Section 4.3 and inference-resource measurements in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The rectified-flow transformer, positional encoding, attention design, view sampling, register tokens, noise schedules, and frame-interpolation component are unchanged. The new video evaluation does not describe an adaptation of the method.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 adds DL3DV-140 evaluation and recorded-video trajectory tests on it and Tanks and Temples. This is a focused extension of existing single-reference scene rendering: DL3DV was already training data, Tanks and Temples already an evaluation benchmark, and the original training mixture and benchmark coverage remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds comparisons against MotionCtrl, VD3D, ViewCrafter, and Wonderland, substantially extending the evaluated comparator set to camera-conditioned video models. Existing NVS and reconstruction comparators remain. CameraCtrl and CameraCtrl II are newly cited but do not participate in Table 3.

E3.justification: The new video protocol uses 300 DL3DV-140 clips and 100 Tanks and Temples clips, one reference frame and 48 subsequent camera poses, COLMAP-based pose estimation and alignment, and image-quality evaluation over the first 14 frames. Appendix D adds single-A100 latency and concurrent-frame-capacity testing at three resolutions, with timing sequences containing one reference and 24 targets. Existing experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a targeted analysis of how inference latency and memory capacity scale with resolution across generative and scene-specific methods. The existing architecture, activation, sampling, and video-pretraining ablations in Section 3 and Appendix A are unchanged.

E5.justification: Point estimates remain the reporting practice. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new clip sample counts and average per-frame timings do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 3 and 8 add substantial camera-control, image-quality, latency, and capacity results. For example, DL3DV-140 rotation error is 0.011 for Kaleido versus 0.061 for Wonderland; at 1024 resolution, Kaleido-Medium and EscherNet take 10.0 and 92 seconds per frame. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under retained settings. Existing NVS, reconstruction, and ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, geometric encoding definitions, sampling distribution, and attention-complexity reasoning are unchanged. The added camera-error evaluation introduces no formal derivations, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified sequence-to-sequence rendering, video pretraining, scalable architecture and training, and strong zero-shot rendering performance. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 explains the overlap with camera-conditioned video generation and why later-frame divergence limits image-similarity evaluation. Appendix D attributes resolution-scaling benefits relative to EscherNet to factorized attention and explains the speed advantage of deterministic rendering. The existing slow-rendering warning and other Section 5 limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents COLMAP processing for the new video evaluation and specifies A100 hardware, sequence composition, and 50-step EscherNet/SEVA versus 24-step Kaleido settings for profiling. These are additional experimental disclosures; the training hyperparameters, training hardware and duration, and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds camera-controlled video references and positions Kaleido relative to their shared single-reference trajectory setting, alongside an additional COLMAP reference. The broader related-work narrative remains intact. Consolidating the rectified-flow preprint citation into its conference version does not remove a distinct prior work.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to the inserted Section 4.3 and Appendix D, an updated evaluation overview, reconstruction paragraph headings, cross-references, and the date. The introduction, method exposition, and conclusion retain their structure and wording.

P2.justification: v2 adds the video-comparison Table 3 and resource-comparison Table 8. The previous reconstruction and appendix tables become Tables 4–7, with modest spacing and page-flow adjustments. Figures 1–10 and the existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 3 adds direct camera-control evidence against relevant video baselines, while Table 8 quantifies inference-cost trade-offs previously discussed qualitatively. These improve empirical support and practical transparency. The gain is limited by image-quality evaluation covering only the first 14 frames and overly broad superiority wording: Wonderland still has better DL3DV-140 LPIPS and slightly better Tanks and Temples SSIM. The original methodological and empirical foundation remains intact.
